strengths: Long, quantitative description and five specific purposes tied to the funded aims
Complete funding record with a correctly formatted NIH award number, amount and project period
Every modality mapped to a recognized standard (OMOP CDM, DICOM, WFDB, EDF+) with schema conformance declared
Per-modality collection protocol with acquisition flags, collector roles and typed raw data sources
Governance clearly distinguishes software licenses from the controlled-access dataset agreement, and source disagreements are recorded with caveats
weaknesses: No IRB approval, informed consent or waiver documentation despite pediatric and neonatal human-subjects data
No DOI, version identifier, errata, publisher or long-term custodian; identifier is a self-minted fragment
No demographic distribution, per-setting counts, or inclusion/exclusion criteria for the 50,000 admissions
Tooling named without versions or repository-level links; no imputation or missing-data documentation
No prohibited or discouraged uses, no reidentification-risk statement, and only a single self-inferred bias entry
recommendations: Populate ethical_reviews.reviewing_organization with the IRB and approval number, and add informed_consent describing the waiver for retrospective records including pediatric/neonatal cases
Mint a DOI, record version and version_access, and name the accountable custodian and repository for the period after 2026-11-30
Report age, sex and race/ethnicity distributions and ICU/PICU/NICU counts from the demographics modality, plus cohort inclusion criteria and the encounter date range
Add per-tool repository URLs and versions for OHNLP, DeGauss, CTP-deid, chorus-extract-upload and the waveform conversion scripts, and document missing-data handling

Add prohibited_uses/discouraged_uses (e.g. reidentification attempts, non-approved commercial use), a participant_privacy.reidentification_risk statement, and additional known_biases entries for measurement and site-documentation heterogeneity
